open_points.subject: staff assignment schema compatibility
open_points.text:
(`staff_id`, `project_id`) is unique among active assignments only, so the
revoked ones of a pair stay (A3 INV-009).
open_points.question: How must this operation handle an existing table created under the former all-records UNIQUE constraint, given that it must provide active-only uniqueness but also "never drops, alters" the table?
options: Permit this operation to migrate or rebuild the old schema and revise the no-alter promise.
Require a deployment-owned migration before this operation and state the current-schema precondition callers must supply.
Detect the old schema and return a specified compatibility failure, narrowing the output guarantee on failure.
open_points.default_guess: Require a deployment-owned migration before startup and make the current-schema version an explicit precondition.

witness.initial: The staff assignment table already exists from the previous release with UNIQUE (`staff_id`, `project_id`) across active and revoked rows, and the pair has one revoked assignment.
events: An administrator later assigns the same staff member to the same project again.
outcomes: The active-only uniqueness obligation permits a new active assignment while retaining the revoked assignment.
The promise to never alter an existing table leaves the former UNIQUE constraint in place, so the new assignment is rejected.
witness.observer: The administrator and the caller of the assignment operation.
